Commentary.Commentary: That ends the second ODI. Australia were not at their best today either but they fought hard towards the end, riding on Shaun Marsh's century. They have not won a bilateral ODI series since beating Pakistan at home in January 2017. Since then, they have lost 0-2 to New Zealand, 1-4 to India and 1-4 to England. Can they keep the series alive in Nottingham? Join us on Tuesday, 19th June, 2018 at 1400 local (1300 GMT) for the third ODI. In the meanwhile, you can catch all the action from the second Windies-Sri Lanka Test as well, going on in St. Lucia. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

JASON ROY HAS BEEN NAMED THE MAN OF THE MATCH FOR HIS 120. Feels relieved to get out of the low-scoring rut. Stresses that there is never any complacency in the English dressing room and every player looks to play well every game. Adds that he was happy to play anchor when Jonny Bairstow was going great guns. On the opening partnership, Roy wishes that there is a consistent opening pair rather than the constant chopping and changing but is quick to admit that he enjoys batting anywhere and with anyone.

Victorious England captain, Jos Buttler, admits that England have won by a good margin but they had to fight hard. Praises Adil Rashid for bowling well at the death when batsmen were going after him and also Plunkett who impressed with a 4-fer. On Jason Roy's knock, he admires the way he paced his innings and reckons England could have got more but Australia bowled well at the death. Is enjoying captaincy but also feels it is a double-edged sword. Is proud of his unit and aims to go 3-0 up in Nottingham.

Australian captain, Tim Paine, feels that 343 was not too many to chase. He says that this can be seen from the way Shaun Marsh played and stitched a wonderful stand with Ashton Agar. Rues the fact that Marsh could not get enough batting partners and reckons that the southpaw can still play a lot of cricket for Australia. Admits that one of the frontline batsmen could have played a bit more and helped Marsh take the team over the line. Is confident that if this side plays at its best, it can still beat England. On being asked about his fitness, Paine says that he is fine now.

Earlier in the day, Australia elected to bowl on an overcast morning but did not bowl well at all. They were forced to play in wet conditions and could not quite adjust to the same. Jason Roy's brilliant 120 did not allow them to pick wickets  in succession but they came back well towards the end to keep England to 342, which could otherwise have seen them rocket to 380. Stay tuned for the presentation.

Not exactly hard for England today but they will feel they could have done better. The bowlers did the hard part by reducing Australia to 110/4 and then would have thought the challenge is over after Maxwell was gone. But then they struggled to bowl consistently during the Agar-Marsh partnership before doing well at the death. Plunkett picked up 4 wickets and was the pick of the bowlers while Rashid's 3 at the death brought England back into the game. Do not forget Moeen Ali's economical 2/47 which stifled the Aussies.

Once again, the top order of the Aussies did not turn up. It just looks odd with three left-handers batting in that top three and England exposed the chink. Travis Head looks out of sorts these days and it was no different today, D'Arcy Short was struggling big time while Shaun Marsh struggled early on. Stoinis and Finch's indifferent form are not helping them either. Even from this position, the lower middle order took them to 300. Just imagine what could happen if the top order contributes more.

So, a victory which never really looked in doubt after England made 342. But Australia did give them a scare. They looked down and out at 110/4 but the 54-run stand between Marsh and Maxwell followed by the 96-run partnership between Marsh and Agar gave the visiting side some hope. However, in the end, England were good enough to brush aside the threats.

OUT! That ends the game. Plunkett finishes with four wickets. A length ball outside off, slower in pace, Jhye Richardson heaves it towards long on where Jason Roy comes running in and takes a brilliant diving catch. ENGLAND WIN BY 38 RUNS AND GO 2-0 UP!!!
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Another googly, outside off, Jhye opens the face of his bat and steers it through point for a single.
Kane Richardson walks in now.

OUT! 100 ODI WICKETS FOR ADIL RASHID! Becomes only the second England spinner after Graeme Swann (104) to reach this landmark. It is reached in the form of a googly which Tye looks to slog out of the park. However, he can only find Sam Billings at the wide long on fence. England are just a wicket away from a 2-0 series lead.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a couple.

FOUR! In the air, could have been caught but Mark Wood has not picked it! A short ball, on middle, Tye pulls this towards deep square leg where Wood is stationed. However, the sun is in his eyes and he fails to pick the ball. Moves away from it and the ball lands in front of the ropes.

Full and outside off, Tye gets down to play the slog sweep but is done in by the googly. He skies it high in the air but three fielders running for the catch cannot get there. Rashid finally gets to the ball and the batsmen take two.
Full and outside off, Tye backs away and hammers it but straight to mid off. Would have been run out had the fielder hit the stumps at the bowler's end but he misses and Andrew gets a single.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a run.
Jhye Richardson walks in now.

OUT! Done in by the slower one! Plunkett has made a mess of Marsh's stumps. Bowls a lovely delivery, full and swinging in, Marsh looks to flick but is done in by the lack of pace on that one. He misses and the ball disturbs the stumps. End of an innings which started sluggishly, then picked up momentum when no one was watching and in the end, gave his side some hope - worthy of an applause. Well played, Shaun Marsh. 131 from 116 balls. Australia need 50 from 26 balls.
Full and on middle, pushed down to long on for a single.
Andrew Tye walks in next.

OUT! Caught next ball! The dropped chance barely matters. A short ball, on middle, Paine swivels and pulls it straight into the throat of Adil Rashid at long leg. He does not drop it. Paine is frustrated with himself. England will breathe with even more relief. Australia might have been dreaming about a win but now, everything depends solely on Marsh. 51 more needed from 28 balls.

DROPPED! Will this prove costly? A length ball outside off, Paine backs away and then slices the ball high in the air. Moeen Ali covers a lot of ground from backward point, gets to the ball, takes the catch, only to palm it down! Two runs taken.
Liam Plunkett is back for another burst.

Another googly, Marsh punches it through the covers where the fielder slides and allows it through, before Willey slides near the fence to keep the batsmen to two. Three braces in that over. The stand is worth 30 from 16 balls.
Googly and a yorker - a combination which is very difficult to find - but Rashid does and Paine somehow squirts it through mid off for one.
Dropped short, pulled through square leg for a run.
On middle, pushed down to long on for a single.
Outside off, this time Tim goes inside out, over cover and gets two more. 58 more needed from 34 balls. Paine moves to 11 from 7 balls.
The googly, on middle, Paine works it through  mid-wicket and takes a couple.
SIX! What a shot! Full and outside off, Marsh backs away and then eases it over wide long off for a maximum! 16 from that over, Wood's figures read 9-1-57-1!
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Nicely done. A short ball, on middle, Paine swivels and hooks it behind square leg for a boundary.
A short ball on middle, pulled through mid-wicket for a run.
On middle and leg, flicked wide of mid-wicket for a couple.
Down the leg side, flicked towards fine leg for a single. Well, a leg bye has been signalled.

WIDE. This was in response to a huge caught behind appeal. Down the leg side, Paine missed his flick and there was a huge noise when the ball went past the bat. Wood asked Paine whether he nicked it and Paine shook his head.
Flicks this one away through mid-wicket for a run. Very bowled by Rashid - 6 runs and a wicket. 6-0-52-2 so far.
Driven towards the mid on region. One run added to the total.
The batsman has driven it through mid off for a couple.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Skipper Tim Paine has come out to bat now.

OUT! STUMPED! Rashid has broken the 96-run stand. England will heave a sigh of relief. That partnership seemed to be taking the match out of their control. Beautiful bowling from Adil Rashid. He gives this plenty of air and then gets it to drift away. Agar is tempted and comes down the track. But then, he is beaten in the flight and misses the ball. Buttler doesn't. Collects and whips off the bails. Buttler and Rashid rejoice. This wicket means so much to them. Didn't look like Australia will come this far after Maxwell got out. Well played, Ashton Agar. He and Marsh have given their team some sort of a chance - if not, at least fought hard. Nice to see some fight shown.
Comes down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! What a shot. A short ball, around middle, Agar backs away and punches it between mid off and cover for a boundary! 14 from the over, Wood's figures read 8-1-42-1!
Excellent slower ball, outside off, SM is early into his pull and is hit on the body. The ball drops down beside the pitch and the batsmen take a leg bye.
WIDE. Down the leg side, Shaun misses his flick. 89 more needed from 50 balls. The stand moves to 90 from 68 balls.
A short ball, on middle, pulled behind square leg for a run.
Outside off, short, cut straight to point.
Down the leg side, tickled fine for a single.
SIX! CRACK! A short ball, on middle, Marsh swings it into oblivion over mid-wicket! 250 UP FOR AUSTRALIA. 92 more needed from 53 balls. Marsh moves to 114 from 105 balls.
Mark Wood is back on. 7-1-29-1 so far.
MISFIELD, FOUR! Short and outside off, Agar cuts it straight to Liam Plunkett at backward point who bends lazily and lets it through. One Yorkshireman (Rashid) glares angrily at another (Plunkett).
Another long hop, heaved towards deep mid-wicket for another single.
Backs away to the leg side, Rashid follows him and Ashton can only chip it towards long off for one.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a run.

Now Agar follows suit, working it towards long on. 'Yours, yours, yours, keep running!' shouts Buttler to Rashid who obeys his skipper. There is a chance of a second but Marsh slips at the striker's end.
Tossed up on middle, Marsh comes down the track and pushes it to long on for a single.
Adil Rashid is back on. 4-0-37-1 so far.
POWERPLAY 3 time. 5 fielders allowed outside the circle till the end.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Dropped short, Agar pulls it through square leg for a boundary.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
WIDE. A short ball down the leg side, Ashton misses his tuck now. Buttler appeals for a catch but it is turned down.
A short ball outside off, Agar looks to cut but misses.
On middle, tucked through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Dropped short now, Agar pulls it over mid-wicket for another boundary. 11 from that over, Root has gone for just 24 in his 4 overs. Not bad, considering the score.
FOUR! Too wide outside off, Agar just lofts it over cover for a boundary.
Full and down the leg side, Marsh looks to sweep but misses. The ball goes off his pads through fine leg and a leg bye is taken.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Dropped short, cut through point for a couple.
Full and outside off, Marsh reaches out to drive and gets a thick outside edge to short third man.
Joe Root is back on.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.

FOUR! A century for Marsh. Gets it with a flick through mid-wicket. Is happy, takes his helmet off and smiles. Agar hugs him. The entire Australian team is on its feet in the dressing room. Well, the match may be gone, but they can take some heart from this knock.
Outside off, Shaun looks to tap and run but then sees it go straight to cover and stops.
FOUR! Full on middle, Marsh just chips it straight back over the non-striker, beating mid on to the boundary! Moves to 97 now and also brings up the 50-RUN STAND.
Down the leg side, whipped through square leg for a single.
Liam Plunkett is back on. 6-1-32-1 so far.
Driven towards the mid off region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Outside off, Agar looks to punch it through the off side but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Comes down the track and Moeen shortens the length. Agar is forced to defend.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a run.

FOUR! Nicely timed. Acres of space on the leg side (probably deliberately kept so), Marsh comes down the track and just eases it through mid-wicket. Comfortable boundary. Moves to 92 from 91 balls. 136 more needed from 82 balls.
On middle and leg, tucked through square leg for a single.
Dropped short, pulled down to long on for a run.
A short ball, on middle, Ashton looks to pull but mistimes his pull back to the bowler.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Down the leg side, tucked towards square leg for a run.
Short again, sliced to third man for a single. 200 UP FOR AUSTRALIA. The current rate is around 5.6 while the required rate has gone above 10.
FOUR! Short and outside off, Agar cuts it behind point for a boundary!
Dropped short, punched down to long off for a run.
Full and straight, driven back to the bowler.
FOUR! Tossed up outside off, Agar leans and lofts it over cover for a boundary. 149 more needed from 92 balls. The stand is worth 30 from 26 balls. Agar moves to 13 from 15.
The arm ball, on middle, defended back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single.
Full on middle and leg, defended back to the bowler.

DRINKS BREAK. Australia going nowhere. The only thing which might be keeping statisticians interested for a while now is Shaun Marsh approaching his century. Tim Paine might not come out to bat at all, so a wicket is all that might separate England from a quick finish.
On middle and off, SM taps it towards point. He sets off for a single but then stutters. But Agar calls him through for a run.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
WIDE. Slips this down the leg side, Shaun misses his flick.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, Marsh looks to flick but the ball goes off the inner half of the bat past short fine leg. Three runs taken.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball for a single.
A short ball outside off, chipped over point for a couple.
David Willey is back on. 5-0-24-0 so far.
Outside off, punched down to long off for one more.
The batsman drives this through the covers for a single.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a run.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a single.

DIRECT HIT WOULD HAVE HAD MARSH. Agar pushed this in front of cover and set off for a quick single. Jonny Bairstow, who is back on the field, quickly got to his right and in one motion, had a shy at the striker's end. Missed it by a mile. Marsh was not even halfway.
Change of angle now. Mark Wood comes in from around the wicket for this final ball.
Another bouncer, Ashton ducks with his bat hanging in the air like a periscope. Luckily for him, the ball sails over.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
A bouncer on middle, Agar ducks.
A short ball on middle and off, Agar backs away and looks to punch but gets a bottom edge which goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Outside off, left alone.

FOUR! An edgy one. Outside off, Marsh looks to defend but then gets squared up. Ends up squirting it through the vacant slip region to third man. 10 runs from the over but the big wicket of Maxwell as well. 2000 ODI runs for Marsh. Australia need 169 more from 114 balls.
Pushes this down to long off for a single to get off the mark.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery for a quick single.
FOUR! Short and outside off, Marsh punches it through the covers for a boundary.
Interesting. Ashton Agar comes in at number 7, ahead of Tim Paine, replacing Maxwell.

OUT! That is the end of Maxwell and perhaps, officially, Australia's chances now. Maxwell backs away to the leg side and Moeen smartly bowls it outside off. However, instead of going inside out, the Big Show looks to go leg side, which means he has to reach out for the ball. Ends up dragging it high in the air. David Willey at long on completes the formalities. The match is almost a formality as well now. 179 more needed from 118 balls. This is the FOURTH TIME that Moeen has removed Maxwell in ODIs - joint most by any bowler against Maxi - along with Morne Morkel.
Tossed up outside off, Maxwell initially looks to go for the big one but then decides to defend.
A short ball, outside off, Shaun pulls it ferociously through mid-wicket and nearly finds Joe Root there. Lands just short.
The batsman failed to make contact and was hit low on the pads. One run added to the total. The umpire signals a leg bye.
The batsman has driven it through mid on.
The ball strikes the batsman very low on the pads. One run added to the total. Leg bye given by the umpire.
Down the leg side, Maxwell misses his clip and the ball hits him on the thigh pads. Takes a quick leg bye.
On a length around off, defended solidly.
Looks to sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. An LBW appeal ensues but that was going down leg. Just a solitary run from that over.
The batsman drives this through the covers.
Very full and outside off, Marsh does not want to take any risk, just stays put and defends.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

NOT OUT. 'Grounded, grounded, grounded, Marais' says umpire Dharmasena on the mic. Flighted outside off, Marsh lunges to defend but the ball spins past the outside edge. Buttler collects the ball and whips the bails off, appealing as well. It is taken upstairs but replays show the foot to be grounded.
Stumping appeal. Is Marsh gone? Referred upstairs...
Full on middle, pushed towards long on for a single.
The batsman opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man. One run added to the total.
Outside off, pushed towards third man for one.
Outside off, driven through mid off for a run.
That has shot up! A length ball outside off, Maxwell looks to hammer it through the off side but suddenly the ball shoots up and goes above the bat.
On middle, tucked through mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. One run added to the total.
Mark Wood is back on.
On middle and leg, flicked towards mid-wicket.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Full on middle, driven towards mid on.
That ball has taken the inside edge of the batsman and thudded into his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Comes down the track, looks to flick but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. The ball rolls towards the off side and Buttler rushes after it. A single taken.
Short and outside off, cut behind point for a couple.
Moeen Ali is back on. 4-0-14-1 so far.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads for a single.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! That helps. The batsman, that is. A short ball outside off, Maxwell swings hard but gets a top edge. Over the keeper's head it goes, to the third man fence.
Outside off, coming in sharply, Shaun looks to let it go initially but at the last moment, gets his bat down to steer it to third man for a single.
Huge LBW appeal, turned down. Full and straight, Marsh missed his flick and was hit on the pads. Plunkett appealed but the umpire stayed put. Hawk Eye shows it to be missing leg.

FOUR! This time he goes over. Maxwell makes a pre-meditated movement down the leg side and Rashid floats this wide outside off. Immediately Maxwell gets to the pitch of the ball and lofts it inside out over cover. 199 more needed from 150 balls now. 12 from the over, Rashid has gone for 37 in 4 overs.
Uppish, but safe! Full and outside off, Glenn looks to go inside out but mistimes his shot. The ball lands short of mid off.
On middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a brace.
Full and outside off, driven towards cover.
Down the leg side, clipped past short fine leg for a couple.
FOUR! CLUNK! There goes Maxwell. Jumps down the track and sends it over mid on. One bounce and into the fence. 207 more needed from 155 balls.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off, Marsh crashes it past a diving point fielder and gets a boundary.
On middle, jumps up onto the batsman, Glenn pushes it uppishly but it is wide of the bowler. A quick single taken to mid on.
FOUR! CLUBBED! A long hop, on middle, Maxwell swivels and pulls it behind square leg for a boundary.
Full and outside off, sliced straight to point.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full on middle, driven back to the bowler.
On middle and leg, tucked towards mid-wicket. 10 from that over, Rashid's figures read 3-0-25-1.

Full and outside off, Marsh comes down the track and drives it towards long off. Substitute Tom Curran comes charging in and has some work to do. Maxwell wants the second but Marsh says no. Now because there is such a loud communication, it attracts Curran's attention. He does the crime of looking up to see what is the drama and in the process, misses the ball. Even now, Marsh is not sure whether the second should be taken but Maxwell stamps his authority and calls him through.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, driven towards long off for a single.
Long on comes up.
Same shot, this time it is along the ground and to the left of the cover fielder. Alex Hales manages to get to the ball from sweeper and keeps the batsmen to three.
FOUR! Nicely done. Tossed up outside off, Marsh dances out, gets to the pitch of the ball and chips it over cover for a boundary. 226 more needed from 167 balls.
Nope. No maiden this time. Maxwell helps it through mid-wicket for a couple.

A length ball down the leg side, Maxwell misses his tuck and is hit on the pads. He sets off for a single before realizing that the ball is just beside him and the bowler is running in quickly. Can Plunkett get his second maiden of the match?
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Another dot. It is outside off, Maxwell just pushes and misses.
On middle, pushed towards mid on.
Full on off, driven towards mid off.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off for a single. 8 runs and a wicket from that over, Rashid's figures read 2-0-15-1.
Glenn Maxwell comes in at number 6, replacing Finch. A last ray of hope, if any, for the visitors. Batting is getting increasingly difficult with the pitch tiring down and also taking spin.

OUT! Stone dead. Aaron Finch here in front of the wickets and Australia in this run chase. Very full, on middle, Finch gets down to paddle but misses and is hit on the pads. That always looked out and as soon as the bowler appealed, the umpire raised his finger. Finch had a chat with his partner but then was sent on his way by Marsh who would have just asked - 'Did you hit it'? A duck for Finch, his 8th in ODIs, half of them coming against this opposition.
On middle, flicked towards mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! 13th ODI Fifty for Marsh. Gets a bit of a gift from Rashid, a high full toss, the southpaw comes down the track and heaves it over mid-wicket. It is a miscue but in the gap.
Around off, defended back to the bowler.

Lucky to get away with that. Marsh comes down the track a bit prematurely but is beaten in the flight. Rashid tosses this wider and Shaun goes through with the shot, over the off side. Slices it through point for a couple. 238 more needed from 179 balls.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
A short ball now, defended stoutly.

FOUR LEG BYES. Down the leg side, Finch looks to tuck it fine but misses. However, the ball kisses his thigh pads and shoots to the fine leg fence. 100 UP FOR AUSTRALIA, but at a much slower rate than they would have wanted.
Aaron Finch comes in next, at number 5, replacing Stoinis.

OUT! Nothing Stoinis could have done about that. The ball pitched on a length outside off, he looked to defend from the crease but the ball just shot low, took the bottom edge and cannoned into the stumps. Stoinis stands there in despair before trudging off. Such things happen when the pitches get drier. Tough luck for Stoinis. Australia sink deeper - 244 more needed from 183 balls.
Full and outside off, Stoinis takes his bat out of the way.
Around off, coming in, defended to the leg side.
Liam Plunkett is back on. 2-0-14-0 so far.
Full and around off, pushed towards mid on but the bowler himself rushes to collect.
A short ball, outside off, this one skids through as well. Marsh goes back to cut but is taken aback by the zip. Manages to get it behind point for a couple though.
Full on middle, MS just thrusts his bat to defend. The ball skids through, takes the inside edge and goes to deep mid-wicket. A run taken.
WIDE. The googly again, but this is down the leg side. Marcus cannot quite connect with his attempted flick.
Floated outside off, Stoinis lofts this inside out over cover for a couple. 248 more needed from 189 balls.

Interesting. Nasser Hussain observed Shaun Marsh's dismissal in the first match. After that he asked Ricky Ponting whether this has something to do with the southpaw's technique or whether he gets genuinely good balls most often. To that, Punter replies that batters look to move away from the ball in order to play the inside out shot. He adds that Marsh should get habituated to getting closer to the ball rather than moving away.
The googly outside off, punched towards extra cover.
A touch short on middle, punched down to long on for a single.
Bowling change. Adil Rashid is brought into the attack now.
Tossed up around middle and leg, eased down to long on for one.
Marsh defends this one off the front foot onto the ground.

There's some issue with the ball and the umpires are having a look at that. When Marsh hit the biggie, someone in the crowd stretched his arms but failed to grab that. Perhaps post that, it might have landed on some rough surface. The umpires have taken the opportunity to call for drinks.

SIX! Excellent use of the feel from Shaun Marsh. He is quick to get down the track to the pitch of the ball and go through with the extension of the arms for the lofted stroke. Easily clears the long on fence. This is a welcome boundary for the Aussies after 48 deliveries. Interestingly, as soon as the southpaw played that, someone shouted 'catch it'. Not sure who.
Flatter on the pads, wristed away to the on side for one.
MS goes back to this one and punches it to the off side.
Landed around middle and leg on a slower pace, Marcus defends it from the crease.
Leg slip in place now.
Stoinis goes back to this one and works it away through square leg for one.
Stoinis defends this one solidly showing the full face of the bat.
Almost a return catch! Tossed up from round the wicket by Ali, Marsh slinks down the track to play against the spin. The ball goes off the outer half towards long off for a single.
Ali lands it on a length outside off, Marcus goes back, allowing it to turn, before working it away through mid on for one.
Marcus defends this one solidly off the front foot.
Nicely looped up outside off, Stoinis lunges and defends.
Pushed off the front foot to covers for nothing.
Marsh blocks this one off the front foot.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.
Bowled around middle and leg, blocked nicely off the front foot.
Floated outside off, driven through mid off for one.
Root comes from round the wicket and delivers it on the pads. Marcus goes back and tucks it behind square on the leg side for one.
Tossed up outside off, Stoinis gets forward and plays the lap towards fine leg for one.
Marcus Stoinis makes his way out to the middle next for Australia. A slip and a straight mid on in place.

OUT! Short's struggles against spin have become more glaring, if they already hadn't in the Indian T20 League. Ali tosses this up nicely around off, Short hangs on the back foot and looks to push it. The ball spins just a bit and takes the outside edge. It is safely pouched by Root, standing at slip. Wonderful from England and Moeen is yet again among the wickets for them. What is interesting to note about D'Arcy here is today, he wasn't at ease even against the seamers.
Short is struggling to rotate strike now. He finds the man stationed at covers with the drive.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.
Looped up outside off, driven through covers for one.
Jonny Bairstow is now going off. Tom Curran is back on as a sub.

Good work from Bairstow! Tossed up ball in line of the stumps, Marsh gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it nicely down the ground. Jonny hares to his left from long off and does nicely to keep it down to a brace with a slide. However, in the process, he seems to have done his already troubled knee some more damage.
Tossed up around off, driven straight to mid off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Shorter outside off, cut away square on the off side for another single.
Served on the pads, Short works it through square leg and gets to the other end.
Lovely loop on that one, pushed back to the bowler.
Flatter one on the pads, flicked away round the corner for one.
More spin. Joe Root to roll his arm over. Perhaps the presence of two southpaws has mooted this move from Buttler.
Loopy ball outside off, driven through covers to retain strike.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. One run added to the total.
Marsh pushes it towards mid off for a single.

Dropped? Seems so. Tom Curran the culprit. Tossed up on the stumps, Marsh slinks down the track and whips it straight to mid-wicket. Curran the substitute, fluffs the chance. Even earlier, Bairstow had grassed an opportunity of Shaun. Can he make England pay?
Flatter outside off, punched away through covers to get to the other end.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Another on around middle, flicked away to mid-wicket for nothing.
Plunkett comes round the wicket and bowls it around off. Marsh defends it from the crease.
On the pads again, flicked away through square leg for a brace.

Excellently done by Wood. Plunkett errs in line and delivers it on the pads. Marsh just tucks it away fine. The ball seems to be headed to the fence, before Mark rushes to his left and puts in a sliding effort. He does well and keeps the batters to two, it seems. Numerous replays roll in and find that the fielder has done just well. Leg byes signalled by the umpire.
There is a good diving effort at the fine leg fence. Mark Wood is the fielder. It's taken upstairs for a check.
Huge appeal, for nothing. Length ball, a touch shorter. Marsh arches back to play the cut but gets hit on the pads. The English appeal to no avail. An inside edge is detected on the replays.
Full on the stumps, Marsh drives it down the ground. Ali runs to his left from mid off and cuts it off.
Flatter on the stumps, defended from the crease. Decent beginning for Ali.
Tossed up outside off, driven through covers for one.
Floated full on the stumps, driven right back.
Short and flat outside off, cut away through backward point for one. The batters think about the second but that's not on.
Spin is not Short's strength and the first sign of that is seen here. He goes back to block it but ends up punching it aerially towards covers. Goes on the bounce to the man there.
Oh, not the start Moeen would've wanted. Flatter outside off, Marsh punches it to covers. But Roy there misfields, which results in a single.
Time for spin. Moeen Ali comes on now.
POWERPLAY 2 time. 4 fielders allowed outside the 30-yard circle till the 40th over.

One more ball down the leg side, Shaun tickles it past short fine leg, through backward square and takes three runs. Moves to 21 from 25 balls. 12 from Plunkett's first. Decent Powerplay 1 for Australia. 60/1.
Around off, Marsh blocks it to the off side.
Another one down the leg side, flicked aerially through square leg for a single.
FOUR! Not a bad ball to receive when you are struggling. Down the leg side, Short does a repeat of what he did on 9.1. 287 more needed from 243 balls. The stand is worth 32 from 37 balls.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
FOUR! An indifferent start. It is on a length, down the leg side, Short just helps it past short fine leg. Moves to 12 from 18 balls and that is his first boundary.
Liam Plunkett will bowl the final over of Powerplay 1.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off for a run.
Down the leg side, helped to fine leg for a single.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Outside off, punched through point for a couple.
Full and just around off, Marsh squirts it towards cover.
On middle and leg, tucked around the corner for a single. 299 more needed from 251 balls. The stand moves to 20 from 29 balls.

FOUR! CLOBBERED! After missing out on the previous two occasions, Marsh finally executes a pull shot to perfection. This is a rank long hop, around off, Marsh swivels and pulls it with force behind square leg. Fine leg has no chance.
A short ball once more. SM looks to pull but is beaten.
Banged in short, Shaun looks to pull but gets a bottom edge which goes fine. Jos Buttler dives to his right to stop.
Fuller on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
WIDE. This is down the leg side, Marsh misses his tuck.
Half volley outside off, driven straight to cover.
Too straight, defended to the leg side.
Full and outside off, Marsh executes a typical cover drive which is intercepted well by the fielder, parrying it to mid off. A single taken.
A short ball, D'Arcy looks to pull but is hurried onto the shot and mistimes it towards square leg. A run taken.
Full and outside off, Short drives this straight back. Willey bends to field but lets it through his legs. Mid off backs it up.
Down the leg side, helped to fine leg for a single.
FOUR! Insult to injury for the bowler. He drops it short outside off and Marsh cuts it behind point for a boundary.
DROPPED? Perhaps. A length ball on middle and leg, Marsh flicks this powerfully through mid-wicket where Jonny Bairstow dives to his right but cannot hold on.
Tucks this through square leg and gets a couple.
Pushes this down the ground, towards mid on.
Full and around off, Short looks to drive but gets a thick inside back to the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Down the leg side, tucked towards fine leg for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, Short has a hack but misses.

Full and outside off, Marsh gets going and drives it through the covers. Seems good enough to get to the ropes but it is the longest side of the ground. The fielder gets to the ball before it touches the boundary. Three runs taken.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Around off, defended watchfully.

Played to the point region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single. Gets off the mark. A boundary off the first ball, wicket from the next, followed up by 3 dots and a single. 2-0-15-1 for Wood so far.
Full and just outside off, watchful defense back to the bowler.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Around off and outside, defended back to the bowler.
Shaun Marsh comes in at number 3, replacing Head. Really bizarre from Australia. 1,2 and 3 are all southpaws.

OUT! The catch is legal and Head has to depart. Wood strikes. He bowls it on a length, around middle and leg and Head looks to tuck it around the corner. But he struggles to adjust to the extra bounce and just tucks it uppishly. Alex Hales dives to his right from short mid-wicket and takes it cleanly. However, the umpires are not so sure and refer it upstairs. One look is good enough to certify that. Another failure for Head. 319 more needed from 280 balls.
Is that caught now? Head has flicked one straight to mid-wicket but the umpires want to see whether the catch is legal.
FOUR! BRUTAL! Short and wide outside off, Head crunches this through the covers for a boundary!
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
Outside off, a play and a miss.
Full and outside off, driven towards cover.
Full and outside off, Head drives this straight back.
Down the leg side, D'Arcy looks to tuck but the ball goes off his pads towards fine leg. A leg bye signalled.
Outside off, left alone.

NOT OUT. PITCHED OUTSIDE LEG. Does seem like a waste of the review. To the naked eye itself, it looked like pitching outside leg. Hawk Eye just confirms it. Head walked across a touch to tuck it to the leg side but missed and was hit on the pads. Buttler was not sure but the bowler convinced him to go upstairs.
LBW! Or not? Wood convinces Buttler to go for the LBW review against Head. Here we go...
SIX! That is a terrific shot! Banged in short outside off, Head initially looks to duck but then decides to play the upper cut. Gets it over the slips and beyond the ropes!
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Outside off, tucked to fine leg for a single.
Outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Short and outside off, Short looks to punch it through the off side but gets a thick inside towards fine leg. A couple taken.
WIDE. Starts with a wayward ball down the leg side, plenty of swing, Short is not able to put bat on ball.
Mark Wood to bowl with the second new ball.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Not a bad length but bad line. Full and down the leg side, hint of inswing, Head just about gets bat to it to send the ball to the fine leg fence.
On middle and leg, punched straight to mid on.
Outside off, closer to the stumps, TH lets it go.
That is a peach now. Full and outside off, Travis looks to flick but is beaten comprehensively as the ball swings away.
FOUR! Wrong start. Down the leg side, Head just tucks it through fine leg for a boundary!
Welcome back. Barely a break. Short and Head are striding out to the middle. David Willey will start off proceedings to Head. Here we go...
